text:
Alex (PM): Quick sync — I posted a short PRD draft for SLO backfill + retention UX in the Observability Console. Need to lock down acceptance criteria, rollout gating, and a few edge cases.

Priya (Eng): First question — are we backfilling org-level aggregates only, or do customers expect user-level/event-level backfill? cost diff is huge.

Marco (Obs): Draft assumption in the doc is org-level only for automated backfill (90d window). User-level/backfill-by-query would be on-demand and expensive. Edge case: very large orgs (>10M events/day) may need partial backfill windows.

Sam (DevEx): From UX POV we need: progress UI (percent, ETA), ability to cancel, and a cost estimate before starting. Also link to billing docs.

Alex (PM): Proposed acceptance criteria (short):
- API: start/stop/backfill-status endpoints exist
- UI: progress + cancel + cost estimate visible
- Safety: system SLO regression during backfill < 10% vs baseline
- Docs: billing/limits & opt-in flow

Jin (QA): We should define the SLO regression test precisely. Suggest: compare p95 query latency and error rate 7d pre-backfill vs during-backfill window; fail if p95 increases >10% absolute or error rate doubles.

Tara (Ops): Ops concerns: backfills will spike reads and can thrash caches. Operational throttles needed. Proposal: max concurrent backfills per region = 3, plus token-bucket per-account rate limiting. Also require a dry-run mode.

Priya (Eng): Implementation note: we'll stream the backfill to a low-priority lane. Add header `X-Backfill-Priority: low` and route to nodes with degraded scheduling. Also implement checkpointing so partial failures resume.

Alex (PM): Draft SLOs (RFC snippet):
```
SLOs (examples):
- availability: 99.95% over 30d for console API endpoints
- query_p95_latency: < 200ms for list/summary queries (non-backfill)
- backfill_window: support up to 90d backfill per org
- backfill_slo_degradation: < 10% relative increase in p95 latency during backfill
```

Marco (Obs): Edge-case: when storage tiering/compaction has already GC'd raw events older than retention window we should fail the backfill with a clear error: `DATA_UNAVAILABLE_TOO_OLD`. Also report partial counts.

Sam (DevEx): UX addition: show an in-console estimate like: `Estimated cost: $X — includes compute + egress`. If estimate > $5k show an extra confirmation modal. :warning:

Alex (PM): Policy question: do we make backfill self-serve for Hosted customers, or require a sales enable for the first few months? My recommendation: gated (sales enable) for Hosted during initial rollout, self-serve for Dedicated.

Priya (Eng): Gated makes sense to limit blast radius. Dedicated teams can self-serve. Implementation-wise it's a feature flag + entitlement check.

Jin (QA): QA needs: synthetic backfill job + load tests that run while a backfill is active to validate acceptance criteria. I'll add a test plan draft.

Tara (Ops): Also add monitoring: per-backfill metrics (bytes_processed, records_processed, duration, error_count) and an alert if node CPU or p95 increases > threshold.

Alex (PM): OK action items: Priya — API spec + checkpointing approach; Marco — metrics and failure modes + acceptance test specs; Sam — UI mock + copy for cost modal; Jin — QA harness & test cases; Tara — ops runbook + throttles. I'll update PRD with these and request review. Please add comments on the PRD by EOD Thu.

Priya (Eng): I'll open an API RFC branch today.

Marco (Obs): I'll add expected Grafana panels and a list of signals to the PRD.

Sam (DevEx): I'll drop a quick mock in Figma and link it in the doc.

Jin (QA): Noted, will start on harness.

Alex (PM): Thanks — quick follow-up: any objections to the gated rollout approach?

Priya (Eng): No objections.

Marco (Obs): 👍

Sam (DevEx): 👍

Tara (Ops): fine with gated.

Jin (QA): 👍

Alex (PM): Great — I'll post updated PRD link in this thread once done. Thanks all.
